steps.label: Do Now: Follow the Cables (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Follow the Cables (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy might a school put every laptop on a network?Show the answer

So people can communicate and share, for example one printer for the whole class.

4 minutes. From 6.3.1 and 6.3.2. Look at the cables in the picture, then answer.

items.prompt: Can Ben print on the Printer?
items.explain: Ben, then the switch, then the Printer. They are all plugged into the same switch.

items.prompt: Can Dev print on the Printer?
items.explain: Dev has no cable. Nothing joins Dev to the switch, so nothing can travel from Dev.

items.prompt: Can Ana send Chi at school a message?
items.explain: Ana, the switch, then the router. No cable goes from the router to the school switch, so the message cannot get to school.

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: following the cables

steps.text: A different picture. Do the same steps with the Do Now picture.
Can Sam print? Start at Sam. Follow his cable to the switch. Is the Printer plugged into the same switch? Then the data can get there.
Can Max print? Start at Max and look for his cable. There is no cable, so nothing can leave Max.
Can Jo send Kim at the shop a message? Kim is on another network. Follow the cables from Jo to the switch, then to the router. Is there a cable from the router to the shop switch?
steps.visual: Jo → Switch → Router → Shop switch → Kim

steps.text: Now look at the Do Now picture. Start at the sender. Follow each cable, one step at a time. Check every step has a cable.
steps.visual: start at the sender, follow every cable

steps.label: Do Now: Packets and Traces (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Packets and Traces (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does each packet have a number on it?Show the answer

Packets can take different routes and arrive in a different order. The numbers let the computer at the end put them back together.

4 minutes. From 6.3.2 and 6.3.3. Type your answers, then press Check answers.

4.Router G81.2.3.7

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Extension: Do Now Challenge
steps.content:
Extension: Do Now Challenge

Think → Pair → ShareWhy practise old questions before the new slides?Show the answer

Each new slide builds on the last lessons. If you remember them, the new slides are easier.

Extension: only if you finished the Do Now early. More questions on routers and packets. Stuck? Turn on I need help. When the Do Now time is up, press Next.

steps.label: 6.3.R: Computer Networks Review
steps.content:
6.3 Computer Networks

Computer Networks Review

Year 6, 6.3.R

Think → Pair → ShareWhy read every slide carefully today?Show the answer

Nobody is there to explain it. The slide is your teacher today, so everything you need is on it.

  • 1 minute. Today you work on your own. The slides teach you. Read each one, do what it says, then press Next.
  • Each slide says how many minutes it takes. Look at the clock.
  • Then you play Data Bridge 3D: answer questions to earn coins, then build bridges.
  • Stuck in the game? Press Learn mode on its start screen. It shows a worked example and gives free help.
  • Notes: press the pen icon at the top. Write down every fact you get wrong.
  • Done: you reach the last slide and finish the drill.

steps.label: Networks and Switches
steps.content:
Networks and Switches

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "the laptops are next to each other" not enough to make a network?Show the answer

Being close does not join them. Data can only travel if there is a cable or Wi-Fi between them.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • A network is two or more computers that are joined together, by cables or by Wi-Fi.
  • Networks let people communicate (messages, video calls) and share (files, a printer).
  • A laptop has one network socket. A switch has many, so every device plugs into the switch.

items.prompt: Four laptops must be joined. Each has one network socket. What do you need?
items.explain: A switch has many sockets, so every laptop can plug into it.

items.prompt: A class has 20 laptops on a network and one printer. Why is this better than 20 printers?
options: It costs less: they all share one printer
The laptops do not need charging
items.explain: Sharing one printer over the network means the school buys one printer, not twenty.

steps.label: Routers and the Internet
steps.content:
Routers and the Internet

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can a message not go along one cable from Bangkok to London?Show the answer

No one cable goes that far. So data travels a long way one step at a time.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • A switch joins the devices inside one network. A router joins networks together.
  • The internet is many networks joined to each other by routers, all round the world.
  • The path data takes is its route. Each router receives the data, then sends it on to the next one.

items.prompt: Which joins the home network to the school network?
items.explain: A router joins different networks and passes data between them. A switch works inside one network.

items.prompt: Look at the picture. How many routers does the message pass through, from Ana to Ben?
items.explain: Home router, Router A, Router C, School router: 4. Ana and Ben are laptops, not routers.

steps.label: Data in Packets
steps.content:
Data in Packets

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is a big photo sent as many small packets, and not in one piece?Show the answer

Many people can share the same cables, taking turns, so nobody waits behind one huge photo.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • Data is split into small parts called packets. Routers send and receive data as packets.
  • Each packet has a number. Packets can take different routes, so they can arrive in a different order.
  • The computer at the end sorts them by number. If one packet is lost, only that one is sent again.

items.prompt: These packets arrive: 2 "is", 3 "fun", 1 "Coding". What is the message?
items.explain: Sort by number: 1 Coding, 2 is, 3 fun.

items.prompt: One packet of a photo is lost on the way. What happens?
options: The whole photo is sent again
Only that packet is sent again
items.explain: Each packet travels on its own, so only the lost packet needs to be sent again.

steps.label: Every Device Has an Address
steps.content:
Every Device Has an Address

Think → Pair → ShareA pizza is going to a house on a long street. Why does the driver need the house number, not only the street name?Show the answer

Many houses are on one street. The number picks out exactly one house.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • Every device on a network has its own address, a number like 192.168.1.3. On the internet it is called an IP address.
  • Data carries the address of the device it is going to. Two devices must never have the same address.
  • In a terminal, type ipconfig to see a computer's IP address.

items.prompt: Look at the picture. A message goes to 10.0.0.4. Which device gets it?
items.explain: Chi's address is 10.0.0.4, so the message goes to Chi.

items.prompt: Ben and Dev both have the address 10.0.0.8. A message goes to 10.0.0.8. What happens?
options: Ben gets it, because he was first
It goes to both, much faster
The network cannot tell which one it is for
items.explain: Two devices with one address: the network cannot tell which one the data is for.

steps.label: Websites, the Web and Traces
steps.content:
Websites, the Web and Traces

Think → Pair → ShareRoads and shops: why are the roads not the same thing as the shops?Show the answer

The roads carry you to the shops. The shops hold the things you want.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • A website is kept on a web server: a computer on the internet with its own address.
  • The World Wide Web is all the web pages kept on web servers. The internet carries them to you.
  • A trace lists each hop on the way to a website: every router, then its web server last.
Trace route to www.park.example
1.Home router192.168.1.1
2.Router A81.2.3.1
3.Router B81.2.3.2
4.Web server203.0.113.25

items.prompt: Read the trace. What is the address of the web server that keeps www.park.example?
items.explain: The last hop is the web server: 203.0.113.25. The other hops are routers.

items.prompt: What is the World Wide Web?
options: All the networks joined by routers
All the web pages kept on web servers
items.explain: The web is the web pages. The networks and routers are the internet, which carries the pages.

steps.label: How to Play Data Bridge 3D
steps.content:
How to Play Data Bridge 3D

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a wrong answer in the game still help you learn?Show the answer

The game shows the reason. If you write it in your notes, you get it right next time.

1 minute. Read the steps. The next slide is the game.

  1. Answer the question in the side panel. Right answers earn coins.
  2. Walk with W A S D. Press B to build the bridge with your coins. Press E to use things.
  3. Ride the cart across. When the light is RED, hold Space to stay in the cart.
  4. The bridge breaks? Answer a new question for more coins, then build again.
  5. Stuck? Press Learn mode on the start screen. It shows a worked example and gives free help. Then go back to Play.
  6. Done: your cart crosses 2 bridges. Then keep playing until the time is up.

steps.label: Data Bridge 3D: Networks
steps.content:
Data Bridge 3D: Networks

Think → Pair → ShareWhy read the whole question before you answer, even when you want to build?Show the answer

A quick wrong answer earns fewer coins. Reading it all first earns more.

9 minutes. Questions from 6.3.1 to 6.3.3. Done: 2 bridges crossed, or the time is up. Then press Next. W A S D walk, B build, E use. RED light: hold Space. Stuck? Learn mode on the start screen.

steps.label: What Is a Search Engine?
steps.content:
What Is a Search Engine?

Think → Pair → ShareThere are millions of web pages. Why can a search still take less than a second?Show the answer

The hard work was done before you asked, so there is much less to do when you search.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • A search engine is a website that finds web pages for you. The words you type are your search terms.
  • It visits web pages all the time and keeps a list of the pages and the words on them.
  • When you search, it looks in its list. It does not read every page again.

items.prompt: You search for tiger. Where does the search engine look?
options: At every web page, one by one, right then
In its list of web pages and their words
items.explain: It looks in its list. It made the list before you asked, so the search is fast.

items.prompt: A new web page about red pandas went online a minute ago. Why might a search not find it yet?
options: The search engine has not visited it, so it is not in the list
Web pages about red pandas are not allowed
The internet is too full today
items.explain: The search engine only finds pages in its list. It adds a new page when it visits it.

steps.label: Best Match First
steps.content:
Best Match First

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a search engine put the best match at the top, and not at the bottom?Show the answer

Most people only read the first few results. The page they want should be where they look first.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • The search engine puts the pages in order, best match first. This is called ranking.
  • Pages with more of your search terms come first.
  • Same number? A search term in the title counts more than one in the text.

options: Greenhill Zoo: Tickets and Opening Times
items.explain: Greenhill Zoo: Tickets and Opening Times has both search terms: zoo and ticket.

items.prompt: The other two pages each have one search term. Why is the Swimming Pool page ranked above the Bus Times page?
options: Its search term is in the title
items.explain: Ticket is in the Swimming Pool page's title. Zoo is only in the Bus Times page's text.

steps.label: Clear Search Terms
steps.content:
Clear Search Terms

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do small words like the and is not help a search?Show the answer

Almost every page has them, so they do not pick out the page you want.

2 minutes. Read the left side. Then answer the questions on the right, and read the reason after each answer.

  • Clear search terms are a few key words that the page you want has.
  • Leave out small words like how, the, is and I. Spell the words right.
  • A word with two meanings needs one more word.

items.prompt: Ben wants to know when Greenhill Library opens. Which search terms are clearest?
items.explain: library opening times: three key words that the library page has. The others have small words, or one word that many pages have.

items.prompt: Look at Kim's search. What should she search for instead?
items.explain: mouse has two meanings, an animal and a computer mouse. One more word, fix, picks the right page.

steps.label: Data Bridge 3D: Searching the Web
steps.content:
Data Bridge 3D: Searching the Web

Think → Pair → ShareWhy use Learn mode when you are stuck, and not guess?Show the answer

A guess teaches you nothing. A worked example shows you how to do the next one.

10 minutes. Questions from 6.3.4. Done: 2 bridges crossed, or the time is up. Then press Next. W A S D walk, B build, E use. RED light: hold Space. Stuck? Learn mode on the start screen.

steps.label: Data Bridge 3D: All of Computer Networks
steps.content:
Data Bridge 3D: All of Computer Networks

Think → Pair → ShareWhy practise every topic together at the end?Show the answer

Mixed questions make you choose which fact to use. That is how a test asks them.

11 minutes. Questions on every topic. Cross as many bridges as you can. Stop 4 minutes before the end and press Next. W A S D walk, B build, E use. RED light: hold Space. Stuck? Learn mode on the start screen.

steps.label: Plenary: Addresses and the Web Drill
steps.content:
Plenary: Addresses and the Web Drill

Think → Pair → ShareWhich fact from today will you check in your notes first, and why?Show the answer

Each person names their own, for example the one they got wrong in the game, because it is the one they do not know yet.

4 minutes. Answer a batch of five. Three right in a row masters a card. Your progress is saved for your teacher. Done: the lesson is over.

y6_3r_do_now_2.feedback: Write the numbers 1 to 6. Which ones did not arrive?
Count only the routers. The last hop is not a router.
Which hop is the web server? Copy its address exactly, dots and all.
